votes.evidence: Premise confirmed by tracing the path. `find_signal_implementation_run` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-514) calls `find_task_run(pr_url=..., branch=..., repository=...)` at api.py:504 and only afterwards checks `run.team_id != team_id` at api.py:505-506, returning None with no second lookup. `find_task_run` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-98) has no team filter: the pr_url leg is `TaskRun.objects.filter(output__pr_url=pr_url)` optionally narrowed by `task__repository__iexact` (webhooks.py:41-43), ordered by terminal_rank then `-created_at` and `.first()` (webhooks.py:47-57); the branch leg filters `branch`, `task__repository__iexact`, `state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True` and takes `.first()` under Meta ordering `-created_at` (webhooks.py:66-76, models.py:1144-1146). `TaskRun` Meta (models.py:1144-1170) declares indexes only, no uniqueness on (pr_url) or (repository, branch), so two teams can hold rows with the same PR URL/branch. The docstring at api.py:489-497 promises "team scoping is enforced here", but the implementation is a post-filter that another tenant's newer or non-terminal row can shadow, so the requested team's own valid run is missed. Cross-team same-repo is a supported configuration: test_webhooks.py:832-836 sets up two teams with the same GitHub installation (`integration_id="555000"`) and asserts resolution picks one. The only caller is stamphog's inbox carve-out (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:189-199), which passes `team_id=repo_config.team_id` and treats None as "not a self-driving PR" (returns `_InboxCarveOut()`), i.e. the legitimate re-review is silently skipped. Existing tests (test_webhooks.py:1259-1318) only cover a single run per case; the `other_team` parameter (line 1292) asserts None for a foreign team_id, never the shadowing case with two runs.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) TaskRun might use a fail-closed team-scoped manager — no, `TaskRun(models.Model)` at models.py:1063 uses the default manager and the facade's own `get_task_run` (api.py:473-480) applies team_id as an explicit filter, so nothing scopes `find_task_run` implicitly. (2) A uniqueness constraint could make the collision impossible — none exists on TaskRun for pr_url or (repository, branch); the only pr_url uniqueness is on CodePrSnapshot (migration 0037:204), a different model. (3) The collision could be unreachable in practice — this is where the finding weakens: `TaskRun.branch` is the checkout/base branch (models.py:1081, `pr_base_branch` at models.py:586, checkout at provision_sandbox.py:677-678), and self-driving PRs use generated head refs, so a cross-team run with `branch == PR head ref` requires another team to deliberately start a run on that branch of the same repo; a cross-team duplicate `output.pr_url` similarly requires another team's run to have worked on or been webhook-bound to the same PR. Both need two PostHog teams sharing one repository, which exists (dogfood, tested at test_webhooks.py:832) but is rare. (4) Impact is fail-closed: the caller falls back to ordinary bot-PR handling (review refused), no cross-tenant data exposure. So the defect is real and the one-line fix (filter by team_id inside the query) is cheap, but the trigger is narrow and the failure mode is a missed automation, not a security or data problem — severity downgraded from should_fix to consider.

The selection is unscoped by team. `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:504` calls `find_task_run(pr_url=pr_url, branch=head_branch, repository=repository)` and only afterwards does `if run is None or run.team_id != team_id: return None` (line 505-506). Neither leg has a `team_id` filter.

2. The docstring at api.py:489-494 promises "the team scoping is enforced here - a run belonging to any other team returns None, and no caller can accidentally bind a PR to another tenant's run". The code delivers the second half (never returns another tenant's run) but not the implied first half (the requested team's own run is found). The existing test `test_non_qualifying_runs_return_none[other_team]` (`products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1292-1310`) only covers "one run in another team returns None"; nothing covers "runs in both teams, the requested team's run must win".

3. Reachability in production: the precondition is a second team holding a `TaskRun` for the same repository with the same `output.pr_url` or the same `branch`. This is a supported configuration, not a hypothetical: (a) GitHub installations map to teams many-to-one - `Integration.objects.first_github_for_team_installation(team_id, installation_id)` and `first_github_for_user_installation` (`posthog/models/integration.py:290-303`) exist precisely because several teams can hold the same installation; (b) `TaskRun` has no uniqueness on `(repository, output.pr_url)` or `(repository, branch)` - `products/tasks/backend/models.py:1063-1160` only defines indexes (`task_run_output_pr_url_idx`, `task_run_wizard_branch_idx`); (c) `branch` and `output` are caller/agent-controlled via `TaskRunUpdateSerializer` (`products/tasks/backend/presentation/serializers.py:167-179`), and a task can be started on an existing `posthog-code/*` branch (`products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/start_agent_server.py:65-71` describes exactly that follow-up shape). So a user in a second team that integrates the same repo, starting a follow-up run on the self-driving PR's branch, yields a same-repo/same-branch (and potentially same-pr_url) row in team B. Because the pr_url leg prefers non-terminal runs (webhooks.py:44-51), team B's IN_PROGRESS run beats team A's COMPLETED self-driving run; the branch leg is unordered `.first()` so it is arbitrary.

It is fail-closed (no wrong approval, no cross-tenant binding), which keeps this at should_fix rather than must_fix. votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) "A repo is owned by exactly one team, so no cross-team rows exist" - false for Tasks: `StamphogRepoConfig` is unique per (installation, repo) (`products/stamphog/backend/models.py:67-69`, oldest-wins in `_resolve_repo_config` tasks.py:289-304), but the Tasks product has no such constraint and the Integration model explicitly supports several teams on one installation (integration.py:290-303). (2) "A PR URL is produced by exactly one run, so the pr_url leg cannot collide across teams" - organically true for the run that opened the PR, but `output.pr_url`/`branch` are writable through the run update API and follow-up runs on an existing branch are a supported flow, so a second team's run can carry the same values; and the branch leg needs only a branch-name match, which follow-up runs reproduce by design. (3) "The stamphog caller rechecks team_id, so nothing bad happens" - the recheck at tasks.py:199 only prevents cross-tenant binding; it does not recover the requested team's run, so the observable defect (skipped self-driving re-review) stands. (4) "Trigger requires a rare multi-team same-repo setup" - narrows blast radius (hence should_fix, not must_fix) but does not make it unreachable; PostHog's own dogfood is a multi-project single-org setup, and the docstring's own contract claims team scoping the query does not implement.
